skill.name: error-handling
skill.description: Guides developers through structured error handling for FastAPI backends and React or Next.js frontends, including custom exceptions, global handlers, logging, and user messages.
skill.summary: Build consistent backend and frontend error handling with custom exceptions, global handlers, logging, and user-friendly API responses.
skill.author: Awais68

security_audit.summary: All static findings were reviewed as false positives caused by Markdown examples, local imports, sample fetch usage, and validation messages. One semantic issue remains: the skill shows internal error details in client-facing API responses, which can disclose implementation details if reused directly.

remediation.issue: Internal error details are shown in API responses.
remediation.suggestion: Keep internal details in server logs, or include them only behind an explicit development-mode guard.

remediation.issue: The frontend error model accepts internal messages from server responses.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the client-facing internal field or document that production responses must omit it.

semantic_findings.title: Internal Error Details Exposed in API Responses
semantic_findings.description: The skill examples include an internal error field in client-facing responses and map it into frontend error objects. This can leak implementation details or identifiers if copied without a debug-only guard.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The backend handler, frontend mapping, and response example all show an internal field reaching the client. A debug comment exists, but the sample does not show an enforcement guard.

content.value_statement: Application errors often become inconsistent, unclear, or unsafe. This skill provides patterns for exceptions, API responses, logging, and frontend messages.
actual_capabilities: Defines backend exception classes with HTTP status codes and user messages.
Shows narrow try-catch patterns and cleanup with finally blocks.
Demonstrates structured logging with correlation IDs and stack traces.
Adds FastAPI global exception handlers for application and unexpected errors.
Maps API errors into frontend messages, toasts, and React Query handlers.
Provides a checklist for status codes, logging, and response consistency.
limitations: Examples require adaptation before production use.
It does not inspect an existing codebase automatically.
It does not replace threat modeling or privacy review.
The sample internal error field needs debug gating before deployment.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Errors
use_cases.description: Create consistent exception classes, status codes, and response messages for a backend service.

use_cases.title: Improve Frontend Feedback
use_cases.description: Map server errors into clear toasts and page states without exposing technical details.

use_cases.title: Review Error Practices
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to find swallowed errors, inconsistent formats, and missing correlation IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Exceptions
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new backend feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design basic application exceptions for my FastAPI feature. Include status codes and user-safe messages.

prompt_templates.title: Add Global Handlers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add global error handlers for known application errors and unexpected errors in my API.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Frontend Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to map API error responses into React user messages, toast notifications, and retry behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my error-handling design for logging, privacy, status codes, retries, and user-facing messages.

output_examples.input: Implement error handling for missing records and validation failures.
output_examples.output: A structured plan with custom exceptions, matching HTTP status codes, safe user messages, and handler placement.

output_examples.input: Improve frontend behavior for failed API requests.
output_examples.output: A mapping from response types to titles, user messages, toast behavior, and retry recommendations.

output_examples.input: Review an error-handling approach before launch.
output: Checks for sensitive data in logs.

best_practices: Separate internal diagnostics from user-facing messages.
Use specific exceptions and narrow try blocks.
Log errors with correlation IDs and redacted context.
anti_patterns: Swallowing broad exceptions without logging or recovery.
Returning stack traces or internal details to production clients.
Using different error response shapes across related endpoints.

faq.question: Does this skill generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples. Review and adapt them before production deployment.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on FastAPI backends and React or Next.js frontends.

faq.question: Can it help with logging?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows structured logging, correlation IDs, and error context patterns.

faq.question: Does it handle business validation?
faq.answer: It supports domain exceptions, but business rules still need product-specific design.

faq.question: How should internal errors be exposed?
faq.answer: Keep internal details server-side in production. Show users a safe and clear message.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
